hypothesis: v0 fails 14+ tasks with empty answers (finish_reason=length at max_tokens=2048 where DeepSeek-V4-Pro exhausts all tokens in hidden chain-of-thought) and 8 tasks with wrong non-empty answers (hallucinated responses to questions requiring live external data). Replacing the flat single LLM call with a deterministic web-signal router (regex) + structured FINAL ANSWER: extractor (regex) + COT at 8192 tokens + 4096-token recovery pass will convert at least 4 empty-or-wrong answers to correct ones on train-30.
changes: From v0 (agent/base.py): (1) system prompt changed from 'output final answer only' to 'work through key steps then FINAL ANSWER: <value>'; (2) max_tokens raised from 2048 to 8192 for primary call; (3) deterministic regex extractor on FINAL ANSWER: marker; (4) 4096-token recovery pass when primary returns empty content; (5) deterministic web-signal regex gate routes matching tasks through a 3-turn DuckDuckGo search pipeline before falling back to COT

hypothesis: At least 4 train-30 tasks (ec09fa32, e142056d, 5f982798, 0a65cb96) fail because DeepSeek-V4-Pro's extended thinking exhausts the 8192-token primary budget AND the 4096-token recovery budget with finish_reason=length and content='' on both passes. Adding a third 'giant-budget' COT pass at max_tokens=32768, triggered deterministically when both prior passes return length+empty, will give enough hidden-thinking room for complex logic tasks (ec09fa32, e142056d) to complete and produce a visible answer.
changes: From mh_iter1_robust_cot_web: (1) added GIANT_MAX_TOKENS=32768 constant; (2) added _is_empty_length() helper that returns True when finish_reason=='length' and content is empty; (3) in _run_cot, after the recovery pass, if both primary AND recovery returned length+empty, add a third 'giant-budget' LLM call using the full SYSTEM_PROMPT (CoT) at max_tokens=32768 — this gives 4x more token budget for DeepSeek-V4-Pro's extended thinking plus visible answer; all other logic (web search pipeline, web signal regex, FINAL ANSWER extractor) unchanged

hypothesis: At least 4 train-30 score-0 tasks (48eb8242, 72e110e7, 16d825ff, 872bfbb1) fail because the mh_iter2 web pipeline provides only DuckDuckGo snippet text (~150 chars per result) to the final LLM answer call, without fetching full page content. In each of these tasks the relevant source URL appears in the search results but its body is never read, causing the LLM to answer from insufficient context (wrong answer or empty). Adding a deterministic URL-fetch step after SEARCH2 — selected by Python string matching on domain tokens from the task prompt, falling back to the first snippet URL — and injecting up to 4000 chars of fetched body text into the SEARCH_ANSWER call will raise train-30 acc from 0.40 to 0.43+.
changes: From mh_iter2_robust_giant_budget: (1) added _url_fetch() helper that fetches a URL via urllib, strips HTML tags, returns up to 4000 chars, emits tool.called/tool.returned events; (2) added _select_best_url() that extracts all URLs from combined SEARCH1+SEARCH2 snippets and deterministically prefers domain-matched URLs (domain token appears in task_prompt) over first-URL fallback; (3) in _run_web_search(), after SEARCH2 web results are obtained, call _select_best_url() + _url_fetch() on the selected URL and append the fetched body as 'Full page content from top result (URL):' in context3 before the SEARCH_ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT LLM call; all other logic (web signal regex, FINAL ANSWER extractor, COT passes, giant-budget pass) unchanged

hypothesis: At least 3 train-30 score=0 tasks (bec74516, 9b54f9d9, 4d0aa727) fail because extras.file_name is set but the agent never reads the locally-cached GAIA attachment files — instead the LLM sees '[Note: this task references a file ... which is not provided in this baseline run.]' and either refuses or hallucinates. Adding a deterministic Python file-reader (openpyxl for xlsx, xlrd+zipfile for xls-in-zip, text read for jsonld/xml/csv) that replaces the loader placeholder with actual file content will move file-reading out of the LLM and into Python, enabling these tasks to be answered correctly. Expected acc: 0.4333 → 0.5000+ (2–3 new correct answers).
changes: From mh_iter3_robust_url_fetch: (1) added _GAIA_FILE_CACHE_BASE constant (HF snapshot path); (2) added _find_gaia_file() helper that globs HF cache snapshots for the named file; (3) added _strip_xml_tags() helper (regex, no LLM); (4) added _extract_xlsx_bytes() helper using openpyxl; (5) added _extract_xls_bytes() helper using xlrd; (6) added _read_file_text() dispatcher: xlsx→openpyxl, zip→zipfile+inner-file dispatch (xml→strip_tags, xls→xlrd, xlsx→openpyxl, txt/csv/json→text), jsonld/json/txt/csv/pdb→text read, image/audio→return '' (capability gap); (7) added _inject_file_content() that replaces the loader's '[Note: ...not provided]' placeholder with '[Attached file: <content>]'; (8) in run_task(), before routing: if extras.file_name set → find in cache → read text → inject into task_prompt → emit file.read event; routing re-evaluated on enriched prompt so jsonld ORCID URLs trigger WEB_SEARCH; image/audio emits agent.blocked(model_capability_gap); all other logic (web search pipeline, FINAL ANSWER extractor, COT passes, giant-budget pass) unchanged

hypothesis: At least 4 train-30 tasks (853c8244, 72e110e7, 16d825ff, 114d5fd0) fail because _run_web_search selects exactly ONE URL via _select_best_url and never retries when the fetch returns empty (SSL cert error) or low-quality content. In task 853c8244, the correct MetMuseum exhibition URL appears in search2 results but is never tried because chinahighlights.com (search1 result) was selected first and returned empty due to SSL failure. In 114d5fd0, the UCL book PDF (search2 result #3) was available but the lower-ranked uclpress.co.uk was tried instead. Adding quality-gated multi-URL fetch (search2 URLs first, up to 4 attempts) with SSL bypass will increase successful page fetches and raise train-30 acc from 0.4667 to 0.50+.
changes: From mh_iter4_robust_file_reader: (1) added _MIN_FETCH_LEN=300 and _MAX_CSS_RATIO=0.05 and _MAX_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=4 constants; (2) added _passes_quality_gate() helper — returns True iff len(text)>=300 and css_char_ratio<5%; (3) added _extract_ordered_urls(web2, web1) helper — returns deduplicated URL list with search2 URLs before search1 URLs; (4) modified _url_fetch() to use ssl._create_unverified_context() so HTTPS sites with cert issues are reachable; (5) replaced single _select_best_url + _url_fetch call in _run_web_search with a loop over _extract_ordered_urls()[:4], calling _url_fetch on each and stopping at first that passes _passes_quality_gate(); all file-reading logic (iter4), COT passes, giant-budget fallback, web signal router unchanged

hypothesis: In at least 3 train-30 tasks (16d825ff, 853c8244, 114d5fd0), the multi-fetch loop stops at the first quality-gate-passing URL even though that page is clearly task-irrelevant (busbud.com CSS for a Tri-Rail question, Vogue CSS for a Met Museum question, chomsky.info 1967 essay for a 2019 UCL book page-11 question). No task-relevant content from these pages reaches the web_answer LLM, so it fabricates. By adding a deterministic relevance gate that checks whether ANY quoted string or named domain from the task prompt appears in the fetched text, the loop skips irrelevant quality-passing URLs and continues to the next candidate (up to 8 attempts), reaching task-relevant pages that appear later in the candidate list.
changes: From mh_iter5_robust_multifetch: (1) added _MIN_SIGNAL_LEN=4 constant; (2) added _extract_relevance_signals(task_prompt) — extracts quoted strings (4-80 chars) and explicit domain names from the task prompt as distinctive signals; (3) added _passes_relevance_gate(text, signals) — returns True if any signal appears in fetched text (case-insensitive); empty signal list defaults to True; (4) raised _MAX_FETCH_ATTEMPTS from 4 to 8; (5) changed multi-fetch loop: after quality gate passes, also check relevance gate — if relevance fails, record as best_quality_only fallback and continue to next candidate URL; if relevance passes, select URL immediately (emits source.selected event with gate='quality+relevance'); if no relevance-passing URL found within 8 attempts, fall back to first quality-only URL (gate='quality_only_fallback', preserves iter5 behavior); all other logic (file reader, web signal router, FINAL ANSWER extractor, COT passes, giant-budget pass) unchanged

hypothesis: In at least 3 train-30 score-0 tasks (ec09fa32, e142056d, 0bb3b44a), both the 8192-token primary CoT pass and the 4096-token recovery pass exhaust their budgets with finish_reason=length and empty content. The subsequent giant_budget (32768-token) either times out with APITimeoutError (ec09fa32, e142056d) or produces a wrong answer due to incorrect step-by-step computation (0bb3b44a). These tasks are amenable to compact Python programs: a Markov chain simulator, a minimax enumerator, or a lookup table. Inserting a CODE_GEN stage between recovery and giant_budget — where the LLM writes Python code executed in a subprocess — will solve at least 2 of these tasks, raising train-30 acc from 0.50 to 0.57+.
changes: From mh_iter6_robust_relgate: (1) added CODE_GEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT constant instructing LLM to write a self-contained Python program printing ONLY the final answer; (2) added CODE_GEN_MAX_TOKENS=4096 constant; (3) added _run_code_gen(task_prompt, log, root) function: calls LLM with code-gen prompt, extracts Python from markdown fences or raw content, executes in subprocess(timeout=30), emits tool.called/tool.failed events, returns stdout; (4) in _run_cot(), when both primary AND recovery return length+empty, call _run_code_gen BEFORE giant_budget — if it returns non-empty output use it as the answer, skipping giant_budget; if empty, fall through to giant_budget unchanged; all other logic (file reader, web signal router, relevance gate, multi-URL fetch, FINAL ANSWER extractor, COT passes) unchanged

hypothesis: In at least 3 train-30 score-0 tasks (0512426f, 872bfbb1, 5f982798), _run_web_search's final web_answer LLM call returns finish_reason=length with empty content — DeepSeek-V4-Pro exhausts all 4096 SEARCH_MAX_TOKENS in hidden chain-of-thought before producing any visible output. When this happens, _run_web_search returns '' and run_task discards all web search context (snippets, fetched page content), falling back to bare _run_cot(task_prompt). This bare CoT then hallucinates or also hits length failures. Adding a deterministic retry at WEB_ANSWER_RETRY_MAX_TOKENS=8192 (same messages3 context, doubled budget) when finish_reason=length+empty is detected will keep the full web context and give the model enough room to emit a visible answer, raising train-30 acc from 0.50 to 0.53+.
changes: From mh_iter7_robust_codegen: (1) added WEB_ANSWER_RETRY_MAX_TOKENS=8192 constant; (2) in _run_web_search(), after the web_answer call (call3/result3), extract answer3 = _extract_answer(...); (3) if answer3 is empty AND _is_empty_length(result3) is True, fire a retry LLM call with the same messages3 at max_tokens=WEB_ANSWER_RETRY_MAX_TOKENS=8192, emit llm.requested/llm.responded with pass_='web_answer_retry', update answer3 from retry; (4) return answer3 (the retry result if non-empty, otherwise still ''); all other logic (file reader, web signal router, multi-URL fetch, relevance gate, COT passes, code_gen, giant_budget) unchanged

hypothesis: In at least 3 train-30 score-0 tasks (08c0b6e9, 05407167, 16d825ff), the current _WEB_SIGNAL_RE routes the task to DIRECT because the question mentions a named content type (a specific film, a specific blog post, a named transit system) without an explicit https:// URL. The LLM then hallucinates from incomplete memory. Adding two targeted patterns — '\bIn\s+the\s+(?:film|movie)\b' and '\bblog\s+post\b' — will redirect 08c0b6e9 ('In the film Goldfinger...') and 05407167 ('blog post on replit.com') to WEB_SEARCH, where 4 confirmed WEB_SEARCH runs got 08c0b6e9 correct ('orange, white') and 1 confirmed WEB_SEARCH+url_fetch run got 05407167 correct ('Format Document'). This single regex extension is the deterministic routing fix; no LLM reasoning changes are made. Expected train-30 acc: 0.4000 (iter5 run) + ~0.0667 (+2 tasks) = ~0.4667.
changes: From mh_iter5_robust_multifetch/base.py: added two new alternatives to _WEB_SIGNAL_RE: (1) '|\bIn\s+the\s+(?:film|movie)\b' — matches 'In the film X' or 'In the movie X' at the start of a sentence, routing 08c0b6e9 to WEB_SEARCH; (2) '|\bblog\s+post\b' — matches any mention of a blog post, routing 05407167 to WEB_SEARCH. Safety: 544b7f0c ('what horror movie does the author cite') does NOT match '\bIn\s+the\s+(?:film|movie)\b' because 'movie' is not preceded by 'In the', so it remains DIRECT and correct. All other logic (multi-URL fetch, relevance gate, file reader, COT passes) unchanged from iter5.

hypothesis: Replacing 'output your best estimate' with a CANNOT ANSWER escape in SEARCH_ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT will allow the pipeline to fall through to COT for tasks where the fetched page content is irrelevant, raising train-30 accuracy above 0.50.
changes: Single prompt change to SEARCH_ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT: removed final sentence 'If the search results are insufficient, output your best estimate.' and replaced with 'If the provided content clearly does not contain the specific data needed to answer the question, output EXACTLY on its own line: CANNOT ANSWER'. Added _CANNOT_ANSWER_RE regex, _is_cannot_answer() helper, and a detection block after result3 in _run_web_search() that emits agent.cannot_answer event and returns '' on match. All other logic identical to mh_iter5_robust_multifetch.

hypothesis: Three train-30 tasks (05407167, 08c0b6e9, 16d825ff) route to DIRECT in iter10 and produce hallucinated answers because _WEB_SIGNAL_RE has no pattern covering blog post references, film scene queries, or specific month-day-year date queries. The LLM has wrong or incomplete training data for these specific facts and hallucinates confidently: 05407167 gets 'Delete All Empty Lines' (correct: 'Format Document'), 08c0b6e9 gets 'white' (correct: 'orange, white'), 16d825ff gets '5:23 PM' (correct: '6:41 PM'). Adding three regex patterns to _WEB_SIGNAL_RE will route these tasks to WEB_SEARCH. Unlike iter9 (which tried film/blog patterns on iter5 base and scored 0.3667 vs iter5's 0.4000), iter10's CANNOT_ANSWER escape in SEARCH_ANSWER_SYSTEM_PROMPT makes these routing additions safe: if web content is irrelevant, CANNOT_ANSWER fires and the pipeline falls back to COT — identical to current DIRECT behavior, no regression. train-30 acc expected to rise from 0.5333 to at least 0.5667 (+1 task).
changes: From mh_iter10_robust_cannot_answer/base.py: added three new alternatives to _WEB_SIGNAL_RE: (1) '|\bblog\s+post\b' routes tasks asking about specific blog post content (catches 05407167 'blog post on replit.com'); (2) '|\bIn\s+the\s+(?:film|movie)\b' routes film scene detail queries (catches 08c0b6e9 'In the film Goldfinger'); (3) '|\b(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+\d{1,2}[,\s]+20\d\d\b' routes specific historical date queries (catches 16d825ff 'May 27, 2019'). All other logic (CANNOT_ANSWER escape, multi-URL fetch, file reader, COT passes, giant-budget) unchanged from iter10.

hypothesis: In 3 train-30 score-0 tasks (ec09fa32, e142056d, 872bfbb1), the giant_budget LLM call raises an API exception (APITimeoutError or RateLimitError after all 10 retries exhausted by chat()), and the current except-block leaves the answer empty. Adding a Python code-generation fallback that runs ONLY in this except-block will allow the LLM to write compact simulation/enumeration code and recover answers for at least 1-2 of these tasks, increasing train-30 acc from 0.60 to 0.63-0.67.
changes: Copied mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend/base.py. Added imports: os, subprocess, tempfile. Added CODE_GEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT, CODE_GEN_MAX_TOKENS=8192 constants. Added _run_code_gen(task_prompt, log, root) function that calls LLM for Python code, extracts from markdown fences, executes via python3 subprocess (timeout=30s), returns stdout. Modified _run_cot() giant_budget except-block to call _run_code_gen as fallback and assign answer from stdout if non-empty.

hypothesis: In at least 4 train-30 score=0 tasks (05407167, 48eb8242, 114d5fd0, 72e110e7), _url_fetch returns content dominated by <script> and <style> block text (JSON-LD metadata, CSS rules, JavaScript code) that fills the chars=4000 truncation limit before any human-readable article text is reached. The current re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', raw) removes HTML tag markers but leaves block content as visible text. The web-answer LLM receives only boilerplate, fires CANNOT_ANSWER, and falls to hallucinating COT.
changes: In _url_fetch: (1) add re.sub(r'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>', ' ', raw, flags=re.DOTALL|re.IGNORECASE) before tag stripping; (2) add re.sub(r'<style[^>]*>.*?</style>', ' ', raw, flags=re.DOTALL|re.IGNORECASE) before tag stripping; (3) change default chars from 4000 to 8000; (4) remove explicit chars=4000 from multi-fetch call site so it uses the new default. All other logic identical to mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend.

hypothesis: Passing the accumulated web context (context3) to COT when CANNOT_ANSWER fires will raise train-30 accuracy above 0.60 by grounding the fallback LLM call with real retrieved data instead of bare question text.
changes: Single change vs mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend: in _run_web_search, the CANNOT_ANSWER block changes 'return ""' to 'return _run_cot(context3, log, root)' and updates the log reason string. The log event 'agent.cannot_answer' is preserved; the web-enriched context3 (search snippets + fetched page) is forwarded to COT instead of being discarded.

hypothesis: Tasks ec09fa32, e142056d, and 0b260a57 all reach the giant_budget stage (both primary 8192-token and recovery 4096-token passes return finish_reason=length with empty content), and all fail there: ec09fa32 hits RateLimitError (empty answer, correct=3), e142056d gets the wrong enumeration (12000, correct=16000), 0b260a57 gets hallucinated data (-1044.744, correct=0.269). For ec09fa32 and e142056d these are pure algorithmic tasks (probability simulation and minimax enumeration) where a short Python program produces the correct answer instantly. Inserting code_gen BEFORE giant_budget will solve these two tasks while failing gracefully for tasks that need external data, raising train-30 acc from 0.60 to 0.67.
changes: From mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend/base.py: (1) added imports: os, subprocess, tempfile; (2) added CODE_GEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT ('write complete self-contained Python, print only the answer, standard library only') and CODE_GEN_MAX_TOKENS=4096; (3) added _run_code_gen(task_prompt, log, root) that calls LLM for code, extracts from markdown fences or raw, executes via python3 subprocess (timeout=30s), returns stripped stdout; (4) in _run_cot(), between recovery-empty and giant_budget: call _run_code_gen() — if non-empty answer returned, use it and skip giant_budget; if empty, proceed to giant_budget as before. hypothesis: In ≥3 train-30 score=0 tasks (48eb8242, bec74516, 16d825ff), the multi-fetch loop stops at the FIRST quality-passing URL even though that page is task-irrelevant (e.g. a unicornfish USGS fact-sheet, a YouTube video). The CANNOT_ANSWER escape fires and the pipeline falls to COT which hallucinates. Task-relevant URLs (American crocodile fact-sheet, ORCID profiles, tri-rail timetable) appear later in ordered_urls — after search2's off-topic top result — but are never fetched because the loop breaks on the first quality pass and CANNOT_ANSWER immediately returns ''. Adding a deterministic retry loop that continues fetching remaining candidate URLs (up to _MAX_CANNOT_ANSWER_RETRIES=3 additional quality-passing attempts) before yielding to COT will reach the relevant pages and allow web_answer to produce a correct answer for at least 2-3 of these tasks, raising train-30 acc from 0.60 to ≥0.67.
changes: From mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend/base.py: (1) added _MAX_CANNOT_ANSWER_RETRIES = 3 constant; (2) added _retry_remaining_urls(task_prompt, combined, ordered_urls, start_idx, log, root) -> str helper that iterates ordered_urls[start_idx:], skips quality-failing pages, calls web_answer (pass_='web_answer_retry') on each quality-passing page, stops after _MAX_CANNOT_ANSWER_RETRIES quality-passing attempts, returns first non-CANNOT_ANSWER answer or ''; (3) in _run_web_search multi-fetch loop: added first_pass_idx tracking variable (set when quality gate passes); (4) in CANNOT_ANSWER block: if first_pass_idx >= 0, call _retry_remaining_urls(start_idx=first_pass_idx+1) before emitting agent.cannot_answer and returning ''. All other logic (web signal routing, file reader, COT passes, giant-budget) unchanged from iter11.

hypothesis: In >=3 score-0 train-30 tasks (05407167, 48eb8242, 16d825ff), the web_answer LLM returns CANNOT_ANSWER because the multi-URL fetch loop (_MAX_FETCH_ATTEMPTS=4) stops at the first quality-passing URL — always from search2 (Wikipedia, generic pages placed first by _extract_ordered_urls) — while the task-relevant search1 URL (blog.replit.com/intel, nas.er.usgs.gov/collectioninfo, media.tri-rail.com) sits at position 5+ in ordered_urls and is never fetched. After CANNOT_ANSWER, the pipeline falls to bare COT which hallucinates. Adding a targeted _try_search1_fallback() that specifically retries up to 2 untried web1 (search1) URLs after CANNOT_ANSWER fires will reach the named-source URLs and allow web_answer to return a correct answer. Expected train-30 acc: 0.60 -> 0.63-0.67.
changes: From mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend/base.py: (1) added _MAX_S1_FALLBACK=2 constant; (2) added tried_urls: set[str] tracking in the main multi-URL fetch loop (records all URLs attempted, not just quality-passing ones); (3) added _try_search1_fallback(task_prompt, combined, web1, tried_urls, log, root) helper that iterates web1 URLs, skips already-tried and quality-failing ones, calls web_answer (pass_='web_answer_s1fb') on each quality-passing one up to _MAX_S1_FALLBACK times, returns first non-CANNOT_ANSWER extracted answer; (4) in the CANNOT_ANSWER block of _run_web_search, calls _try_search1_fallback before emitting agent.cannot_answer and returning ''. All other logic (web signal router, file reader, COT passes, giant-budget) unchanged from iter11.

hypothesis: In 3 train-30 score-0 tasks (ec09fa32, e142056d, 5f982798), primary CoT (8192 tokens) and recovery (4096 tokens) both return finish_reason=length with empty content, then the 32768-token giant_budget call throws APITimeoutError (~900s), leaving the answer empty. These algorithmic tasks (Markov chain simulation, constrained optimization, quantitative paper comparison) are solvable by a compact Python program. iter12 tried the same code_gen-in-except approach but used CODE_GEN_MAX_TOKENS=8192, adding ~250s per task after an already-900s timeout — likely triggering cascading rate-limit failures for the 30-task benchmark run (iter12 train_score=0.3333 vs frontier 0.60). Reducing CODE_GEN_MAX_TOKENS to 1024 (a 8x reduction) limits the fallback call to ~30s, preventing cascading delays while still providing enough token budget for a compact simulation program.
changes: From mh_iter11_robust_wsig_extend/base.py: (1) added imports os, subprocess, tempfile; (2) added CODE_GEN_MAX_TOKENS=1024 and CODE_GEN_SYSTEM_PROMPT constants; (3) added _run_code_gen(task_prompt, log, root) function that calls LLM at 1024 tokens, extracts Python from markdown fences or raw content, executes via python3 subprocess (timeout=30s), returns stdout; (4) in _run_cot() giant_budget except block: after emitting llm.failed, call _run_code_gen() — if non-empty stdout returned, assign to answer.
